artifacts.summary: Full trace of Stage 3.5 Dispatch Prep and all 11 physical dispatch-site call points in skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, the additional per-dispatch inputs orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh must gather (artifact-round resolution, continuation-pointer dual-form normalization, territory, handoff/dispatch_seq threading), the user-decision contract's target files (no existing precedent found), the routing-table-driven scope for the agent-contract sweep, and the .dispatch/ runtime-file registration surfaces including a flagged gap in reaper coverage.

memory_candidates.content: In skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, task-description counts like 'five single-task Stage 4 sites' refer to logical dispatch recipes, not physical text occurrences of 'Run **Stage 3.5**' (there are 8 physical single-task occurrences + 3 MT-4 loops = 11 total, vs. 5+3=8 logical). When a plan/task description gives a site count for this file, verify by grep before trusting the number, since not_started/researching share one recipe and researched/planning share another.

manifest-routing-lib.sh has two deliberately-separate lookup functions: routing_lookup (two-level {op:{task_type:value}} manifest blocks) and routing_lookup_flat (one-level {task_type:value} blocks, e.g. hard_contracts). routing_lookup_flat is NOT a wrapper over routing_lookup with a fabricated op key -- using the wrong one silently corrupts resolution. Both must be called directly (never via command substitution), reading results from $_ROUTE_LAST_VALUE/$_ROUTE_LAST_VIA.

orchestrator-runtime-files.md's ephemeral/durable-provenance split only covers SINGLETON runtime files (overwritten in place or rm -f'd once at Stage 8). A per-dispatch file that accumulates one copy per cycle (e.g. a future .dispatch/{seq}.md) has no existing reaper: reap-session-runtime-files.sh explicitly does not recurse into specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/, and task-lock.sh reap only handles .lock/. Any new per-task growing-file class needs an explicit disposition decision (bulk rm -rf at Stage 8 vs. a new age-based sweep), not an assumption that it fits the existing singleton lifecycle.
